questions.prompt: Which ions are exchanged between two sides of red blood cells in venous blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The erythrocyte anion exchanger swaps bicarbonate and chloride during CO2 transport: bicarbonate exits and chloride enters during systemic tissue uptake.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 1; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which gas is used for estimating of “diffusing capacity of O2” in the lung?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Carbon monoxide is used to estimate diffusing capacity because rapid hemoglobin binding keeps capillary CO pressure very low. The CO2 subscript was rejoined without creating an extra option.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 2; source page 1.

questions.prompt: What is the mean O2 pressure difference (mmHg) across the respiratory membrane during normal and quiet breathing?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional resting mean O2 gradient across the respiratory membrane is approximately 11 mmHg, smaller than the initial entering-blood gradient of 64 mmHg.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 3; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which one the following is correct about ventilation and perfusion in the lungs?
options: The blow flow decreases from top of the lung to bottom
The ventilation increases from top of the lung to bottom
The ventilation to perfusion ratio (V/Q) increases from top of the lung to bottom
V/Q ratio is same for all levels of the lung in upright person
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In an upright lung, absolute ventilation and perfusion both increase toward the base, but perfusion increases more; V/Q therefore decreases toward the base.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 4; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Compared to other gases, which gas has the highest diffusing capacity during exercise?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO2 has much greater solubility and an approximately twentyfold larger membrane diffusion coefficient than O2; its diffusing capacity exceeds the other listed gases in the teaching comparison.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 5; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following leads to an increase in airway resistance?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Cold-air inhalation can increase airway resistance through irritant/bronchoconstrictor mechanisms; it is the intended contrast to the listed bronchodilator mediators.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 6; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is the normal frequency for beating of cilia in mucociliary system?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Human respiratory ciliary beating is commonly in the order of 10–20 Hz, not beats per minute. Measured rates vary by temperature, age and sampling site; a healthy-adult biopsy study reported a mean 12.5 Hz at 37°C.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 7; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following happens during inspiration?
options: The antero-posterior dimension of the chest is decreased.
The vertical dimension of the thorax is increased
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Inspiratory diaphragm contraction expands the thorax, makes pleural pressure more negative and transiently lowers alveolar pressure below atmospheric pressure to draw air inward.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 8; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a form by which CO2 can be transported in the blood?
options: Bound to the amino end groups in hemoglobin
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Carboxyhemoglobin binds carbon monoxide, not CO2. CO2 is transported dissolved, as bicarbonate and as carbamino compounds bound to amino groups.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 9; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which one the following factor does reduce intracellular oxygen consumption?
options: A decrease in intracellular ATP concentration
An increase in tissue blood flow
An increase in intracellular ATP concentration
An increase in intracellular ADP concentration
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: A high intracellular ATP level reduces the demand signal for oxidative metabolism, whereas increased ADP promotes oxygen consumption. Blood-flow changes alone do not define cellular metabolic demand.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 10; source page 3.

questions.prompt: What is the normal value of utilization coefficient for O2 in a normal person?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At rest, reference arterial and venous O2 contents of 20 and 15 mL/dL give extraction (20−15)/20 = 25%.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 11; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which one the following leads to an increase in affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Reduced 2,3-DPG increases hemoglobin's oxygen affinity and shifts the curve left; acidity, raised CO2 and warming shift it right.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 12; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is NOT correct about pulmonary circulation?
options: Vasodilation occurs in response to hypoxia
Supplies blood flow to respiratory zone
Provides blood flow for gas exchange
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Alveolar hypoxia produces pulmonary vasoconstriction, not vasodilation. Pulmonary circulation is low pressure and supplies the respiratory exchange region.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 13; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Wih a duration of 1.5 seconds for inspiration phase, what will be the duration of Ramp Signal?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the traditional ramp model, the inspiratory signal lasts for the inspiratory phase: 1.5 seconds here. Its subsequent off-period is expiration, not part of the ramp.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 14; source page 4.

questions.prompt: What is the cause of “physiological shunt”?
options: Mixing of pulmonary vein blood with bronchial vein blood
A decrease in the cardiac output to half
An increase in VA/Q ratio 2.5 times more than normal amount
A decrease in ventilation/perfusion ratio (VA/Q) to zero
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Zero V/Q produces shunt, but bronchial venous admixture also contributes to physiological shunt. The broad wording therefore permits two mechanisms; the source-selected low-V/Q answer is retained only as provenance.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 15; source page 5.

questions.prompt: The terminal bronchioles are part of ...
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Trachea, bronchi and terminal bronchioles are conducting airways and constitute anatomical dead space. Respiratory bronchioles and alveoli participate in exchange.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 16; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct about blood flow at the "top of the lung" in a healthy person while lying down?
options: Blood flow will only be maintained during systole
There is a continuous blood flow during both systole and diastole
The blood flow is zone-1 type
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The standard supine teaching model has relatively continuous zone-III flow in the previously apical region because the vertical hydrostatic gradient is reduced. Posture redistributes rather than abolishes all regional gradients.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 17; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is correct about “Transpulmonary Pressure (TPP)”?
options: TPP= alveolar pressure minus atmospheric pressure
At the beginning of the inspiration is equal to + 5 cm of water
TPP= pleural pressure minus alveolar pressure
At the beginning of exhalation is equal to – 7.5 cm of water
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Transpulmonary pressure is alveolar minus pleural pressure: approximately +5 cm water at the start of inspiration and +7.5 at end inspiration. The marked negative expiratory value confuses pleural with transpulmonary pressure.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 18; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which one the following is less than others in the lung?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using the conventional adult reference values, ERV is about 1.1 L, below RV (~1.2 L), IRV (~3 L) and IC (~3.5 L). These are teaching values, not fixed values for every individual.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 19; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which one the following is correct about the role of the dorsal respiratory group in medulla?
options: Inhibits the pneumotaxic center in pons
Sends its action potentials to phrenic nerves
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The intended functional answer is inspiratory drive reaching phrenic motor neurons and the diaphragm. DRG activity is not confined to deep inspiration; modern rhythm generation involves broader medullary networks.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 20; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which one the the following neurotransmitter is NOT released from glomus cell in carotid bodies?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The source selects noradrenaline, but primary carotid-body research supports catecholaminergic release/signaling from type I cells during hypoxia. A species-unspecified absolute NOT-released claim is not reliably unique.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 21; source page 6.

questions.prompt: What Is The Name Cell Secreted Surfactant In Bronchiole?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Celera denotes Clara (club) cells, which secrete protective surfactant components in bronchioles. They are distinct from alveolar type II pneumocytes.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 22; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is observed in structure Histology In Respiratory Zone?
options: Areolar Loss Connective Tissue + Erectile Tissue
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The nasal respiratory region has vascular loose (areolar) lamina propria with erectile venous tissue, not dense connective tissue as its defining support. Respiratory Zone here refers to nasal mucosa, not distal alveoli.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 23; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which part of the lung tissue has Nomocyte II?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Nomocyte II is the source's misspelling of type II pneumocyte, an alveolar epithelial cell that produces surfactant.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 24; source page 7.

questions.prompt: In which of the following isn’t observed Goblet Cell?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The recovered second stem line is Goblet Cell. Both the squamous vestibular region and specialized olfactory epithelium normally lack goblet cells; pharyngeal lining also varies by region. The marked vestibule is not a unique answer.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 25; source page 8.

questions.prompt: In which of the following is observed Elastic Fiber In Histology Structure?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Elastic fibers occur in the trachea and in distal lung structures including alveolar ducts; the broad location question has more than one defensible option.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 26; source page 8.

questions.prompt: Which of the following paranasal sinuses open to the apex of bulla ethmoidal ؟
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Middle ethmoidal air cells open on the ethmoidal bulla in the middle meatus.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 27; source page 8.

questions.prompt: All of the following bones participates in the formation of the lateral wall of the nose except?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The vomer forms the inferior/posterior nasal septum rather than the lateral nasal wall.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 28; source page 9.

questions.prompt: All of the following structures are seen in inlet of larynx except?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The vestibular fold lies within the laryngeal cavity, below the inlet. The epiglottis, aryepiglottic folds and posterior arytenoid region bound the inlet.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 29; source page 9.

questions.prompt: Which bone is involved in both the roof and the medial surface of the nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Ethmoid contributes the cribriform nasal roof and perpendicular plate of the septum. Palatine contributes floor/lateral-wall structures, not the requested roof-and-medial-wall combination; the supplied palatine mark is corrected.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 30; source page 9.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the highest structure in the right lung umbilicus?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The right superior lobar (eparterial) bronchus lies above the right pulmonary artery and is the highest listed hilar structure; umbilicus here means hilum.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 31; source page 10.

questions.prompt: The medial surface of the right lung is adjacent to all the following structures except ....
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The aortic arch relates to the left lung; the right mediastinal surface relates to the venae cavae and azygos system.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 32; source page 10.

questions.prompt: Which of the following arteries passes through the foramen in roof of nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The anterior ethmoidal artery reaches the nasal cavity through the roof near the cribriform plate; the sphenopalatine artery enters through the lateral sphenopalatine foramen.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 33; source page 10.

questions.prompt: Which of the following nerve pass through incisive canal ?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The nasopalatine nerve passes through the incisive canal to the anterior hard palate.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 34; source page 11.

questions.prompt: Which of the following muscles is involved in pulling thyroid cartilage downward and forward ؟
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Cricothyroid tilts the thyroid cartilage forward and downward relative to the cricoid, elongating and tensing the vocal ligaments.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 35; source page 11.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the upper and free side of the quadrangular membrane?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The superior free edge of the quadrangular membrane forms the aryepiglottic fold; its inferior edge forms the vestibular ligament.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 36; source page 11.

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles are paralyzed by cutting the recurrent laryngeal nerve except?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Cricothyroid is supplied by the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve; the listed other intrinsic laryngeal muscles are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 37; source page 12.

questions.prompt: In which time of development the second epithelial alveolar cells appear?
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: The course's Langman/E2 timing places type II-cell appearance near the end of the sixth month (about 24 weeks in the book), before full surfactant maturity.

evidence: Respiratory theory — report dated 24 July 2021; printed question 38; source page 12.

questions.prompt: In which period of lungs development alveolar duct appear
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: In the canalicular period, respiratory bronchioles develop and branch into alveolar ducts; pseudoglandular development reaches terminal bronchioles only.
